title: One input can reach the loss along several paths

blocks.text: The graph is intentionally small but contains the central difficulty of autodiff: one value appears more than once. The node v=x×x lists x twice as a parent. The output z=v+x also uses x directly. Treating each node as having only one downstream consumer would lose information.
Run scalar reverse-mode autodiff on a topologically ordered list of (name,operation,parent_names,value). Support input, add, multiply, and tanh; return gradients by name.

A computation graph records values and the operations that produced them. Topological order places parents before children. Reverse-mode differentiation traverses that order backward, applying each operation’s local rule and accumulating contributions at shared parents.

The backward pass starts by assigning gradient one to the scalar output. Reversing the addition sends that one to v and to x. Reversing the multiplication then sends x times the incoming gradient through each of its two input slots. Since both slots refer to the same node, both contributions must be added to x’s existing gradient.

blocks.text: Connect the picture to the mathematics

blocks.caption: The multiplication x×x contains two parent uses of x. The addition contributes a third, direct path. All three derivatives belong to the same input.

blocks.text: The supplied function stores forward values in a name-to-value dictionary and initializes a separate gradient dictionary. It reverses the supplied topological list instead of discovering an order itself. Each supported operation provides local multipliers: one for addition, the opposite input for multiplication, and 1−value² for tanh. The tanh rule uses the saved output value.

The crucial statement uses += rather than assignment. Replacing it with = would overwrite a contribution from another path, and a duplicate parent such as x×x makes that bug visible immediately. This helper implements scalar operations only; tensor shape rules and broadcast reductions belong to additional work. Verify the graph ordering, unique node names, saved values, and accumulated derivatives separately. A numerical finite-difference check is useful for smooth toy graphs, but it does not replace checking structural assumptions.

notes.text: The output’s derivative with respect to itself seeds the reverse pass.
Every occurrence of a parent adds a contribution; it must not overwrite earlier paths.

checks.prompt: For z=x²+x at x=2, what is dz/dx?

explanation.correct: The two multiplication paths contribute 2 each, and the direct addition path contributes 1.
explanation.default: Revisit the stated quantities and units. The two multiplication paths contribute 2 each, and the direct addition path contributes 1.
